source_refs.note: Practice short questions written from Chapter 22 (PDF 88-100, printed 85-97); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice short questions for the whole of Chapter 22 (Hydroxy Compounds), arranged by the chapter's sections, in the style of a 2-mark Board short question. Each answer is a short model answer; small numericals show the working, and a comparison is answered as a table.

blocks.prompt: 1 What are hydroxy compounds? How do alcohols and phenols differ in where the -OH group is attached?
blocks.explanation: Hydroxy compounds are organic compounds with at least one hydroxyl (-OH) group. In alcohols the -OH is attached to an aliphatic carbon; in phenols it is attached to an aryl (aromatic ring) carbon.

book_ref.quote: Alcohols and phenols are hydroxy organic compounds with at least one hydroxyl group attached to an aliphatic or an aryl carbon, respectively.

blocks.prompt: 2 Why were phenol solutions first used in surgery, and why was their use later given up?
blocks.explanation: After Pasteur showed that bacteria exist, from 1867 surgical instruments and wounds were cleaned with phenol solutions; their potent antiseptic action raised patients' survival. But phenol burns healthy tissues, so it was too potent and alternatives were found.

book_ref.quote: After Louis Pasteur's research revealed the existence of bacteria, scientists started cleaning surgical instruments and wounds with phenol solutions in 1867.

blocks.prompt: 3 Give one use each of ethanol and phenol mentioned in the chapter.
blocks.explanation: Ethanol: produced from bio-based materials and used as a biofuel (an alternative to petrol). Phenol: an ingredient in disinfectants such as soaps and hospital disinfectant liquids.

book_ref.quote: Phenol is an ingredient in disinfectants, such as soaps, hospitals disinfectant liquids, etc.

blocks.prompt: 4 What is the functional group and general formula of alcohols? Name the first two members of monohydric alcohols.
blocks.explanation: The functional group is the hydroxyl group (-OH) and the general formula is ROH, where R is an alkyl group. The first two members are methanol, CH₃OH, and ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH.

book_ref.quote: Hydroxyl group (-OH) is the functional group of all alcohols.

blocks.prompt: 5 Why is C₆H₅OH not classed as an alcohol even though it contains an -OH group?
blocks.explanation: In C₆H₅OH the -OH group is bonded to a carbon of the aromatic ring (aryl carbon). Such a compound is a phenol. In an alcohol the -OH is on an alkyl (aliphatic) carbon, i.e. R in ROH is alkyl.

book_ref.quote: When the -OH group is bonded to an aryl (aromatic ring) carbon the compound is a phenol, not an alcohol

blocks.prompt: 6 Differentiate between monohydric and polyhydric alcohols with one example of each.
blocks.explanation: They differ in the number of -OH groups:

book_ref.quote: Depending on the number of hydroxyl groups attached, alcohols can be classified into monohydric and polyhydric alcohols.

blocks.prompt: 7 Give the IUPAC names of glycol and glycerol and state how many -OH groups each has.
blocks.explanation: Glycol is 1,2-ethanediol (two -OH groups). Glycerol is 1,2,3-propanetriol (three -OH groups). Both are polyhydric alcohols.

book_ref.quote: they are 1,2-ethanediol and 1,2,3-propanetriol

blocks.prompt: 8 On what basis are alcohols classed as primary, secondary and tertiary? Give the general formula of each.
blocks.explanation: On the number of carbon atoms directly attached to the carbon that carries the -OH group: one carbon gives a primary (1°) alcohol, R₁CH₂OH; two give a secondary (2°) alcohol, R₂CHOH; three give a tertiary (3°) alcohol, R₃COH.

book_ref.quote: Depending on the number of carbon atoms which are directly attached to the carbon that is bonded with the -OH group

blocks.prompt: 9 Classify propan-1-ol, propan-2-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol as primary, secondary or tertiary.
blocks.explanation: Propan-1-ol, CH₃CH₂CH₂OH: primary (the -OH carbon has one carbon attached). Propan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₃: secondary (two carbons). 2-methylpropan-2-ol, (CH₃)₃COH: tertiary (three carbons).

book_ref.quote: A tertiary (3°) alcohol is one in which the OH group is attached a tertiary carbon atom.

blocks.prompt: 10 What is meant by saying that alcohols have a low degree of dissociation? Write the equilibrium.
blocks.explanation: In water, alcohol molecules split up into ions only to a small extent: ROH(aq) ⇌ RO⁻(aq) + H⁺(aq). The equilibrium lies to the left, so there are far more ROH molecules than RO⁻ and H⁺ ions.

book_ref.quote: This means that when dissolved in water, alcohol molecules do not dissociate (split up) to a great extent.

blocks.prompt: 11 Show from [H⁺(aq)] that alcohols are weaker acids than water.
blocks.explanation: Both ROH ⇌ RO⁻ + H⁺ and H₂O ⇌ OH⁻ + H⁺ lie to the left, but water gives more H⁺ ions. Alcohols have a lower [H⁺(aq)] than water, so they are weaker acids than water.

book_ref.quote: As alcohols have a lower [H⁺(aq)] in solution compared to water, alcohols are weaker acids than water.

blocks.prompt: 12 What is a positive inductive effect? Which group in alcohols shows it?
blocks.explanation: Electron-donating species push electrons into a covalent bond; this is called a positive inductive effect. In alcohols the alkyl group is electron donating and shows it.

book_ref.quote: Electron-donating species push electrons into a covalent bond and are said to have a positive inductive effect.

blocks.prompt: 13 Give reason: the alkyl group makes ethanol less acidic than water.
blocks.explanation: The electron-donating alkyl group pushes electron density onto the O of the ethoxide ion (CH₃CH₂O⁻). This destabilises the ion, so it readily accepts H⁺ and re-forms ethanol. Hence ethanol ionises less than water.

book_ref.quote: The alkyl groups destabilize the alkoxide ion, which is formed by removing one proton (H⁺) from the alcohol molecule.

blocks.prompt: 14 What is the conjugate base of phenol? Why is it stable?
blocks.explanation: The phenoxide ion, C₆H₅O⁻. One lone pair on its oxygen overlaps with the delocalised π system of the ring, so the negative charge is spread over the ring; this delocalisation stabilises the ion.

book_ref.quote: The delocalisation stabilises the phenoxide ion, the conjugate base of phenol.

blocks.prompt: 15 Why does the phenoxide ion re-form phenol less readily than the ethoxide ion re-forms ethanol?
blocks.explanation: In phenoxide the charge is delocalised into the ring, leaving less charge density on O, so H⁺ is not strongly attracted. In ethoxide the alkyl group increases electron density on O, so H⁺ is strongly attracted back.

book_ref.quote: The H⁺ ions are, therefore, not strongly attracted to the phenoxide ion and are less likely to reform the phenol molecule.

blocks.prompt: 16 Compare the acidity of phenol and ethanol in a table.
blocks.explanation: Phenol is more acidic than water, and ethanol is less acidic than water:

book_ref.quote: The relative acidities are as follows: phenol > water > ethanol

rows: O lone pair delocalised into the ring; less charge on O
Alkyl group donates electrons; more charge on O
Conjugate base stabilised; H⁺ not strongly attracted back
Conjugate base destabilised; readily takes H⁺ back

blocks.prompt: 17 Name the five kinds of compounds from which alcohols can be prepared.
blocks.explanation: Alkenes, halogenoalkanes, carbonyl compounds (aldehydes and ketones), carboxylic acids and esters.

book_ref.quote: Alcohols can be prepared from alkenes, halogenoalkanes, carbonyl compounds, carboxylic acids, and esters.

blocks.prompt: 18 How is ethanol made from ethene? Write the equation and name the type of reaction.
blocks.explanation: Ethene is reacted with hot steam using concentrated H₃PO₄ as catalyst: CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O → CH₃CH₂OH. It is an electrophilic addition reaction.

book_ref.quote: When hot steam is reacted with an alkene, using concentrated phosphoric acid (H₃PO₄) as a catalyst, electrophilic addition takes place to form an alcohol.

blocks.prompt: 19 What type of alcohol is formed when an alkene is treated with cold, dilute KMnO₄? Name the role of KMnO₄ here.
blocks.explanation: A diol (an alcohol with two -OH groups) is formed, e.g. ethene gives 1,2-ethanediol. Cold, dilute KMnO₄ acts as a mild oxidising agent.

book_ref.quote: Alcohols are obtained by the oxidation of alkenes with cold, dilute KMnO₄, a mild oxidising agent.

blocks.prompt: 20 Write the equation for the preparation of ethanol from bromoethane and name the type of reaction.
blocks.explanation: Bromoethane is heated with aqueous NaOH: CH₃CH₂Br + NaOH → CH₃CH₂OH + NaBr. The -OH replaces the halogen in a nucleophilic substitution reaction.

book_ref.quote: The halogen atom in halogenoalkanes can be substituted by –OH group when heated with aqueous NaOH in a nucleophilic substitution reaction, giving an alcohol.

blocks.prompt: 21 What type of alcohol is obtained by reducing (i) an aldehyde (ii) a ketone? Give one example of each.
blocks.explanation: With NaBH₄ or LiAlH₄: (i) an aldehyde gives a primary alcohol, e.g. ethanal → ethanol; (ii) a ketone gives a secondary alcohol, e.g. propanone → propan-2-ol.

book_ref.quote: Aldehydes and ketones can be reduced by reducing agents such as NaBH₄ or LiAlH₄ to obtain alcohols.

blocks.prompt: 22 How is ethanoic acid converted into ethanol? Which class of alcohol is formed?
blocks.explanation: Ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH, is reduced by LiAlH₄ to ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH. Carboxylic acids give primary alcohols.

book_ref.quote: Similarly, carboxylic acids are reduced by LiAlH₄ to primary alcohols.

blocks.prompt: 23 What is formed when ethyl ethanoate is heated with dilute acid? Write the equation.
blocks.explanation: It is hydrolysed to ethanoic acid and ethanol: CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O → CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH.

book_ref.quote: When an ester is heated with dilute acid or alkali, hydrolysis takes place and a carboxylic acid and alcohol are formed.

blocks.prompt: 24 Differentiate between the reduction products of aldehydes and ketones.
blocks.explanation: Both are reduced by NaBH₄ or LiAlH₄, but the class of alcohol differs:

book_ref.quote: Aldehydes are reduced to primary alcohols. Ketones are reduced to secondary alcohols.

blocks.prompt: 25 Write the balanced equation for the complete combustion of ethanol. Why is ethanol used as a fuel?
blocks.explanation: CH₃CH₂OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O, ΔH°c = −1367 kJ mol⁻¹. The reaction is highly exothermic, so ethanol is used as an alternative to petrol in some countries.

book_ref.quote: Alcohols when ignited, undergo complete combustion to form carbon dioxide and water.

blocks.prompt: 26 ΔH°c of ethanol is −1367 kJ mol⁻¹. How much heat is released when 0.30 mol of ethanol burns completely?
blocks.explanation: Heat released = moles × 1367 kJ mol⁻¹ = 0.30 × 1367 = 410.1 kJ (≈ 410 kJ).

book_ref.quote: The above reaction is highly exothermic; this is why the alcohol is used as an alternate to petrol in some countries.

blocks.prompt: 27 How many moles of O₂ are needed, and how many moles of CO₂ are produced, when 0.25 mol of ethanol burns completely?
blocks.explanation: From CH₃CH₂OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O: O₂ = 0.25 × 3 = 0.75 mol; CO₂ = 0.25 × 2 = 0.50 mol.

book_ref.quote: Alcohols when ignited, undergo complete combustion to form carbon dioxide and water.

blocks.prompt: 28 What is meant by substitution of an alcohol? Write the reaction of ethanol with HCl.
blocks.explanation: The -OH group is replaced by another substituent such as a halogen, giving a halogenoalkane. CH₃CH₂OH + HCl → CH₃CH₂Cl + H₂O, with ZnCl₂.

book_ref.quote: In the substitution of alcohols, a hydroxy group (-OH) is replaced by another substituent (e.g. halogens) to form a new product (e.g., halogenoalkanes).

blocks.prompt: 29 Write the reaction of ethanol with sodium. Which bond breaks?
blocks.explanation: 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂(g). The O-H bond of the hydroxyl group breaks; sodium ethoxide (a base) and hydrogen gas form.

book_ref.quote: When an alcohol reacts with a reactive metal such as sodium (Na), the oxygen-hydrogen bond in the hydroxly group breaks.

blocks.prompt: 30 How can sodium metal be used as a test for the hydroxy group?
blocks.explanation: Sodium is added to the compound. If an -OH group is present, the O-H bond breaks and bubbles of hydrogen gas are released; on evaporating excess alcohol a white crystalline sodium alkoxide is left.

book_ref.quote: Bubbles of hydrogen gas are released if a hydroxy group is present.

blocks.prompt: 31 How does phenolphthalein show that sodium reacts more slowly with ethanol than with water?
blocks.explanation: Sodium forms a base in both. With ethanol and phenolphthalein the pink colour forms slowly; with water it appears immediately. So Na reacts more slowly with ethanol.

book_ref.quote: It shows that reaction of Na with ethanol is slower than with water.

blocks.prompt: 32 Arrange methanol, ethanol and propan-1-ol in order of decreasing vigour of reaction with sodium. Give reason.
blocks.explanation: Methanol > ethanol > propan-1-ol. The longer the hydrocarbon chain in the alcohol, the less vigorous its reaction with sodium.

book_ref.quote: The longer the hydrocarbon chain in the alcohol, the less vigorous the reaction becomes.

blocks.prompt: 33 How many moles of hydrogen gas are released when 0.40 mol of ethanol reacts with excess sodium?
blocks.explanation: 2CH₃CH₂OH + 2Na → 2CH₃CH₂ONa + H₂: 2 mol ethanol give 1 mol H₂, so H₂ = 0.40 ÷ 2 = 0.20 mol.

book_ref.quote: If the excess ethanol is evaporated off after the reaction, a white crystalline solid of sodium alkoxide is left.

blocks.prompt: 34 Write the oxidation of ethanol and of propan-2-ol, naming the products.
blocks.explanation: Ethanol (primary): CH₃CH₂OH + [O] → CH₃CHO + H₂O, giving ethanal (an aldehyde). Propan-2-ol (secondary), on heating: CH₃CH(OH)CH₃ + [O] → CH₃COCH₃ + H₂O, giving propanone (a ketone).

book_ref.quote: Primary alcohols can be oxidised to form aldehydes and the secondary alcohols can be oxidised to form only ketones using oxidizing agents.

blocks.prompt: 35 Differentiate between primary and tertiary alcohols in their behaviour towards acidified K₂Cr₂O₇.
blocks.explanation: Only the primary alcohol is oxidised:

book_ref.quote: Tertiary alcohols do not undergo oxidation.

rows: Orange Cr₂O₇²⁻ reduced to green Cr³⁺

blocks.prompt: 36 How is acidified potassium dichromate(VI) used to test for primary or secondary alcohols?
blocks.explanation: Warm the alcohol with acidified K₂Cr₂O₇. Primary and secondary alcohols are oxidised and the orange Cr₂O₇²⁻ ions are reduced to green Cr³⁺ ions. A tertiary alcohol gives no colour change.

book_ref.quote: which is used to check the presence of primary or secondary alcohol

blocks.prompt: 37 Why must potassium dichromate(VI) be acidified to oxidise an alcohol?
blocks.explanation: To act as an oxidising agent the dichromate itself is reduced (Cr₂O₇²⁻ → Cr³⁺). This reduction requires H⁺ ions, which the acidic medium provides.

book_ref.quote: This reduction requires hydrogen (H⁺) ions which are provided by the acidic medium.

blocks.prompt: 38 What is a breathalyser and on what principle does it work?
blocks.explanation: A device used by traffic officers to check whether a driver is drunk. Ethanol in the breath is oxidised; the electrons it releases make a current, and the current is proportional to the amount of alcohol consumed.

book_ref.quote: A breathalyser is a device that is used by the traffic officers to check if a driver is drunk or not.

blocks.prompt: 39 Define dehydration of alcohols. Write the equation for ethanol and name two dehydrating agents.
blocks.explanation: Dehydration is an elimination reaction in which a water molecule is removed from the alcohol to form an alkene: CH₃CH₂OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O. Dehydrating agents: aluminium oxide, conc. sulphuric acid, conc. phosphoric acid.

book_ref.quote: Dehydration is the type of the elimination reaction in which a water molecule is removed.

blocks.prompt: 40 Differentiate between dehydration of ethanol and its oxidation.
blocks.explanation: Both remove atoms from ethanol but give different products:

book_ref.quote: Alcohols can also undergo dehydration to form alkenes.

rows: Reagent: Al₂O₃, conc. H₂SO₄ or conc. H₃PO₄
Reagent: acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ or acidified KMnO₄

blocks.prompt: 41 What are phenols? Give the formula and two other names or uses of the simplest phenol.
blocks.explanation: Phenols are compounds in which a hydroxyl group is bonded to an arene. The simplest is C₆H₅OH, a crystalline white solid; it is also called carbolic acid and was used as carbolic soap.

book_ref.quote: Compounds in which a hydroxyl group is bonded to an arene called phenols.

blocks.prompt: 42 Why is nitrous acid prepared in situ, and how?
blocks.explanation: HNO₂ is so unstable that it cannot be stored. It is made in the test-tube from sodium nitrite and dilute HCl, keeping the temperature below 10°C with ice: NaNO₂ + HCl → HNO₂ + NaCl.

book_ref.quote: The HNO₂ is so unstable that it needs to be prepared in a test-tube by reacting sodium nitrite (NaNO₂) and dilute hydrochloric acid (HCl)

blocks.prompt: 43 Write the equation for the last step in the preparation of phenol from phenylamine.
blocks.explanation: The diazonium salt solution is warmed with water and decomposes (is hydrolysed): C₆H₅N₂⁺Cl⁻ + H₂O → C₆H₅OH + N₂ + HCl.

book_ref.quote: Phenol is made by warming the diazonium salt solution with water

blocks.prompt: 44 Give reason: the diazonium salt is warmed with water, not with NaOH, to obtain phenol.
blocks.explanation: In alkali the phenol formed would change into phenoxide, which couples with the remaining diazonium ions to give an azo dye instead of phenol. With water the salt simply gives phenol, N₂ and HCl.

book_ref.quote: In alkali the phenol would form phenoxide and couple with the remaining diazonium ions to give an azo dye.

blocks.prompt: 45 Why can phenols take part in two kinds of reactions? Name one reaction of each kind.
blocks.explanation: Both the polar OH group and the electron-rich benzene ring can react. OH group: reaction with NaOH to give sodium phenoxide and water. Ring: bromination with bromine water to give 2,4,6-tribromophenol.

book_ref.quote: Phenols can undergo many types of reactions as both the electron-rich benzene ring and the polar OH group can participate in chemical reactions.

blocks.prompt: 46 Give reason: phenol is only slightly soluble in water but dissolves in aqueous NaOH.
blocks.explanation: The large non-polar benzene ring makes phenol only slightly soluble in water. Being slightly acidic, it reacts with NaOH in an acid-base reaction to form the soluble salt sodium phenoxide and water: C₆H₅OH + NaOH → C₆H₅ONa + H₂O.

book_ref.quote: Phenols are only slightly soluble in water due to the large non-polar benzene ring.

blocks.prompt: 47 Write the balanced equation for the reaction of molten phenol with sodium. What type of reaction is it?
blocks.explanation: 2C₆H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₆H₅ONa + H₂. It is an acid-base reaction; the soluble salt sodium phenoxide forms and hydrogen gas is given off.

book_ref.quote: Molten phenols react vigorously with reactive metals such as sodium (Na).

blocks.prompt: 48 How many moles of H₂ are given off when 0.50 mol of phenol reacts completely with sodium?
blocks.explanation: 2C₆H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₆H₅ONa + H₂: 2 mol phenol give 1 mol H₂, so H₂ = 0.50 ÷ 2 = 0.25 mol.

book_ref.quote: it is drawn as 2 phenol + 2Na -> 2 sodium phenoxide + H2

blocks.prompt: 49 Write the reaction of phenol with ethanoyl chloride and name the type of product.
blocks.explanation: Heated in the presence of a base: CH₃COCl + C₆H₅OH → CH₃COOC₆H₅ + HCl. The product, phenyl ethanoate, is an ester.

book_ref.quote: The product, phenyl ethanoate (CH₃COOC₆H₅), is an ester, not an ether

blocks.prompt: 50 Why is a base added when phenol reacts with an acyl chloride?
blocks.explanation: The base deprotonates phenol: C₆H₅OH + OH⁻ → C₆H₅O⁻ + H₂O. The phenoxide ion is a better nucleophile than phenol and attacks the carbonyl carbon of the acyl chloride.

book_ref.quote: The phenoxide ion is a better nucleophile than the original phenol molecule and will be able to attack the carbonyl carbon.

blocks.prompt: 51 Give reason: the -OH group activates the benzene ring of phenol.
blocks.explanation: One lone pair of the oxygen atom overlaps with the π system of the ring and becomes delocalised, increasing the electron density of the ring. The ring is therefore more likely to undergo electrophilic attack.

book_ref.quote: Due to the increased electron density, the benzene ring is more likely to undergo electrophilic attack and becomes activated.

blocks.prompt: 52 Differentiate between the nitration of phenol with dilute and with concentrated nitric acid.
blocks.explanation: The strength of the acid decides how many -NO₂ groups enter:

book_ref.quote: When concentrated HNO₃ is used, the product will be 2,4,6-trinitrophenol instead.

blocks.prompt: 53 What is observed when bromine water is added to aqueous phenol? Name the product.
blocks.explanation: The orange bromine water is decolourised and a white precipitate forms at room temperature. The product is 2,4,6-tribromophenol (electrophilic substitution at the 2, 4 and 6 positions).

book_ref.quote: Phenol decolourises the orange bromine solution to form a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.

blocks.prompt: 54 Differentiate between the bromination of benzene and of phenol.
blocks.explanation: Phenol's activated ring reacts far more easily:

book_ref.quote: Benzene will undergo bromination only when reacted with pure bromine (not a solution) and in the presence of anhydrous aluminium bromide (AlBr₃) catalyst at room temperature.

rows: More reactive: ring activated by the -OH group

blocks.prompt: 55 Why is 1-naphthol called a phenolic compound? Where do electrophiles attack it?
blocks.explanation: 1-naphthol has an -OH group attached to position 1 of naphthalene (an aromatic ring). Like phenol, its -OH is electron-donating and activates the ring; electrophiles are directed to the 2 and/or 4 positions.

book_ref.quote: Just like with phenol, the -OH group in 1-naphthol is also electron-donating and activates the naphthalene ring to electrophilic substitution reactions.
